traps.what: The note's figure: a 2024 Transport Workforce Resilience Council study of 1,850 drivers said to show debriefing within 72 hours cut psychological injury claims by 64%. Neither the body nor the study can be found.
traps.pass: The answer flags the 64% figure as unverified (score_rnd.py NOT_VERIFIED on the same line or sentence) and never labels a row that names it sourced.

traps.what: One-sided support: the provider's own case studies and staff feedback forms from one trial session. Neither measures post-traumatic stress or claims against a comparison group.
traps.pass: At least two sourced Case against rows with passing citations, none of them a URL used in the Case for.

known_against.what: Cochrane systematic review, Rose, Bisson, Churchill and Wessely (CD000560, 2002; earlier versions 2000 and 2001): single-session individual debriefing did not reduce distress or prevent PTSD, one trial found raised PTSD risk, and compulsory debriefing should cease.

evidence.quote: Compulsory debriefing of victims of trauma should cease.

known_against.what: Meta-analysis, van Emmerik, Kamphuis, Hulsbosch and Emmelkamp, The Lancet 2002, 360: 766-771: critical incident stress debriefing (CISD) did not improve PTSD symptoms or natural recovery.

evidence.quote: CISD and non-CISD interventions do not improve natural recovery from psychological trauma.

known_against.what: Randomised controlled trial, Mayou, Ehlers and Hobbs, British Journal of Psychiatry 2000, 176: 589-593 (reprinted in FOCUS 2003): at three years the debriefed group did worse; debriefing is ineffective with adverse long-term effects.

evidence.quote: Psychological debriefing is ineffective and has adverse long-term effects. It is not an appropriate treatment for trauma victims.

known_against.what: Randomised controlled trial of 236 trauma survivors, Sijbrandij, Olff, Reitsma, Carlier and Gersons, British Journal of Psychiatry 2006, 189: 150-155: neither emotional nor educational debriefing reduced PTSD symptoms; emotional debriefing worsened symptoms for high-arousal participants.

evidence.quote: Our study did not provide evidence for the usefulness of individual psychological debriefing in reducing symptoms of PTSD

known_against.what: NICE guideline NG116, Post-traumatic stress disorder (2018), recommendation 1.6.5: do not offer psychologically-focused debriefing for the prevention or treatment of PTSD (the replaced guideline CG26, 2005, said the same about routine single-session debriefing).

evidence.quote: Do not offer psychologically-focused debriefing for the prevention or treatment of PTSD.

evidence_checked: Each evidence URL fetched by check_urls.py on 8 November 2026 between 16:00 and 16:30 AEST: HTTP 200, no soft 404, page holds the quote. check.py repeats this live.

rules.R1: Every cited URL passes check_urls.py: fetched with HTTP 200, not a soft 404, and the page holds the quote. Critical.
rules.R2: Every row of both tables has a label from labels; a sourced row has a URL and a quote.
rules.K1: At least one sourced Case against row cites a known_against URL (matched by URL prefix after the scheme and a leading www. are removed, never by a word pattern) and its citation passes check_urls.py.
rules.L1: Every sourced Quote is max_quote_words words or fewer.
rules.M1: The One-month test section is present and holds at least 20 words.
rules.A1: One rough artefact (a Word file) is saved in the run folder, or the run's notes say why it could not be saved (a fail).

pass: Three fresh-chat runs, each scored with score_rnd.py --key evals/rnd/holdout-v4/answer-key-holdout-v4.json. Malformed output fails (missing section, renamed column, unknown label, no table). Otherwise pass needs T1, T2, R1, R2, K1, L1, M1 and A1. One critical failure fails the round. All three runs must pass.
counter_metric: Words of output (output.md). A run that games K1 by stacking citations grows the answer; the word count must not rise more than 10% against the version's tier-2 baseline.
